• 6+ years of professional experience designing and implementing optimization solutions in production environments.

• Hands-on production experience with OR-Tools (CP-SAT), or a comparable constraint-programming / mixed-integer-programming solver.

• Strong foundation in linear programming, integer programming, or stochastic optimization.

• Direct experience modeling and solving workforce or resource scheduling problems.

• Experience working with large datasets and solving large scale optimization problems.
Proficiency in Java, Python, or C++.

• Experience translating complex business requirements into mathematical models and optimization objectives.

• Strong software engineering skills with the ability to build production-ready services and validation frameworks.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Delivery companies have always bought capacity by guesswork. Book too few drivers and parcels wait; book too many and you pay for empty vans. Most carriers accept that waste as the price of being reliable. Relay is building a marketplace where it isn't. You can't schedule drivers. You can only design what's on offer, and measure what happens.

Every part of our network runs on decisions. The next two years are about building the systems that make them well, and proving they do. Engineering and operational research build what you design.

MARKETPLACE HIGHLIGHTS

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what Marketplace changes on booking, matching and shifts, and recommend on pay. Our scientists' models and experiments feed your calls, and the squad lead acts on them.

title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

- Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

- Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

- Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

- Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

- Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

- Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

- Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers.

- Can build and debug the code behind a training experiment, from preparing data to checking whether a change in the results reflects a real change in model behavior.

- Enjoy working through ambiguous cases with domain experts and translating what you learn into concrete decisions about how a model should respond.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.
